<br />

Use the Console API to write messages to the Console from your JavaScript. See [Get started with
logging messages to the Console](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/log) for an interactive introduction to the topic.

[Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=76U0gtuV9AY)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key point:** DevTools assigns a severity level to most of the `console.*` methods. These levels allow you to filter logged messages. For more information, see [Filter by log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level).

See [Console utilities API reference](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/utilities) if you're looking for the convenience methods like `debug(function)` or
`monitorEvents(node)` which are only available from the Console.

## console.assert(expression, object)

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Error`

Writes an [error](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api#error) to the console when `expression` evaluates to `false`.

    const x = 5;
    const y = 3;
    const reason = 'x is expected to be less than y';
    console.assert(x < y, {x, y, reason});

![The result of the console.assert() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consolea-da55a23b35561.png)

## console.clear()

Clears the console.

    console.clear();

If [**Preserve Log**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#persist) is enabled, `console.clear()` is disabled.

Alternatively, you can [Clear the Console](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#clear) by clicking the ![ALT_TEXT_HERE](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/alttexthere-03849da35a84e.svg) icon.

## console.count(\[label\])

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Info`

Writes the number of times that `count()` has been invoked at the same line and with the same
`label`. Call [`console.countReset([label])`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api#countreset) to reset the count.

    console.count();
    console.count('coffee');
    console.count();
    console.count();

![The result of the console.count() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consolec-6204ede77c5f4.png)

## console.countReset(\[label\])

Resets a count.

    console.countReset();
    console.countReset('coffee');

## console.createTask(name)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key point:** This method is known as the Async Stack Tagging API. If you use a framework or abstraction for scheduling and async execution that already uses this API under the hood, you don't need to call this API directly.

Returns a `Task` instance that associates the current stack trace with the created `task` object. You can later use this `task` object to run a function (`f` in the following example). The `task.run(f)` executes an arbitrary payload and forwards the return value back to the caller.

    // Task creation
    const task = console.createTask(name);

    // Task execution
    task.run(f); // instead of f();

The `task` forms a link between the creation context and the context of the async function. This link lets DevTools show better stack traces for async operations. For more information, see [Linked Stack Traces](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/devtools-modern-web-debugging#linked_stack_traces).

## console.debug(object \[, object, ...\])

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Verbose`

Identical to [`console.log(object [, object, ...])`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api#log) except different log level.

    console.debug('debug');

![The result of the console.debug() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consoled-7423f935aeec2.png)

## console.dir(object)

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Info`

Prints a JSON representation of the specified object.

    console.dir(document.head);

![The result of the console.dir() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consoled-e78c6d6869a14.png)

## console.dirxml(node)

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Info`

Prints an XML representation of the descendants of `node`.

    console.dirxml(document);

![The result of the console.dirxml() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consoled-9c8e1488e3a93.png)

## console.error(object \[, object, ...\])

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Error`

Prints `object` to the Console, formats it as an error, and includes a stack trace.

    console.error("I'm sorry, Dave. I'm afraid I can't do that.");

![The result of the console.error() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consolee-0343ccd08a048.png)

## console.group(label)

Visually groups messages together until `console.groupEnd(label)` is called. Use
`console.groupCollapsed(label)` to collapse the group when it's initially logged to the Console.

    const label = 'Adolescent Irradiated Espionage Tortoises';
    console.group(label);
    console.info('Leo');
    console.info('Mike');
    console.info('Don');
    console.info('Raph');
    console.groupEnd(label);

![The result of the console.group() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consoleg-776ad95204ea1.png)

Additionally, you can nest groups.

    const timeline1 = 'New York 2012';
    const timeline2 = 'Camp Lehigh 1970';
    console.group(timeline1);
    console.info('Mind');
    console.info('Time');
    console.group(timeline2);
    console.info('Space');
    console.info('Extra Pym Particles');
    console.groupEnd(timeline2);
    console.groupEnd(timeline1);

![Nested groups.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/nested-groups-b33070a206428.png)

## console.groupCollapsed(label)

Same as [`console.group(label)`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api#group), except the group is initially collapsed when it's logged to
the **Console**.

## console.groupEnd(label)

Stops visually grouping messages. See [`console.group`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api#group).

## console.info(object \[, object, ...\])

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Info`

Identical to [`console.log(object [, object, ...])`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api#log).

    console.info('info');

![The result of the console.info() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consolei-2d6e3caa7c6d5.png)

## console.log(object \[, object, ...\])

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Info`

Prints a message to the Console.

    console.log('log');

![The result of the console.log() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consolel-3503077b72fe7.png)

## console.table(array \[, columns\])

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Info`

Logs an array of objects as a table.

    var people = [
      {
        first: 'René',
        last: 'Magritte',
      },
      {
        first: 'Chaim',
        last: 'Soutine',
        birthday: '18930113',
      },
      {
        first: 'Henri',
        last: 'Matisse',
      }
    ];
    console.table(people);

![The result of the console.table() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consolet-deafe365f75ef.png)

By default, `console.table()` logs all table data. To display a single column or a subset of columns, you can use the second optional parameter and specify column name or names as a string or an array of strings. For example:

    console.table(people, ['last', 'birthday']);

![A subset of columns in a table logged with console.table().](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/a-subset-columns-a-tabl-d09038277395f.png)

## console.time(\[label\])

Starts a new timer. Call `console.timeEnd([label])` to stop the timer and print the elapsed time to
the Console.

    console.time();
    for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) {
      let square = i ** 2;
    }
    console.timeEnd();

![The result of the console.time() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-console-2603011443558.png)

## console.timeEnd(\[label\])

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Info`

Stops a timer. See [`console.time()`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/api#time).

## console.trace()

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Info`

Prints a stack trace to the Console.

    const first = () => { second(); };
    const second = () => { third(); };
    const third = () => { fourth(); };
    const fourth = () => { console.trace(); };
    first();

![The result of the console.trace() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consolet-526ce53ae5c57.png)

## console.warn(object \[, object, ...\])

[Log level](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/reference#level): `Warning`

Prints a warning to the Console.

    console.warn('warn');

![The result of the console.warn() example above.](https://developer.chrome.com/static/docs/devtools/console/api/image/the-result-the-consolew-2de7ba6ff12cc.png)
